findings.title: [P2] Preserve uncertainty when Decimal canonicalization underflows
findings.body: The local context increases precision but retains the default exponent limits and leaves Underflow untrapped. Consequently, `canonical_number("1e-1000100")` passes the finite-float checks, then multiplication and normalization silently turn the nonzero Decimal into `"0"`. A QML origin with latitude `0` and an SCML origin with latitude `1e-1000100` can therefore receive `same_record_content=true`; with matching creationInfo and a recovered pick, this also permits a false recorded-revision resolution count. Preserve the exact value or return an unknown geometry field when arithmetic is inexact, rather than treating underflow as matching content. Python documents these context-dependent rounding rules in its [Decimal documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/decimal.html#decimal.Decimal.normalize).

overall_explanation: Decimal canonicalization can silently collapse distinct geometry values and enable claims that violate the conservative comparison contract. Review was read-only; no tests or acquisition were run.
